cor:affine-line.cautions: This is birational rationality after affine-line stabilization, not Zariski cancellation for isomorphic affine cylinders.
cor:affine-line.conclusion: Each displayed cubic yields a nonrational smooth projective fourfold Y for which Y times A1 is rational.
cor:affine-line.hypotheses: X is either displayed cubic threefold and Y is X times P1.
cor:affine-line.objects: The smooth projective fourfold Y and its affine-line stabilization.

cor:cubics.cautions: This is restricted to the two Tschinkel--Zhang series, not every smooth cubic hypersurface.
cor:cubics.conclusion: X times P2 is rational over Q for every member of either series.
cor:cubics.hypotheses: r is nonnegative and X is one of the cubics in Tschinkel--Zhang Propositions 5.1 or 5.3.
cor:cubics.objects: The two explicit series of cubic hypersurfaces.

cor:finite-index-chow.cautions: Degree-one cycles are supplied by rational points in the domain of a parametrization. The proof resolves rational maps, moves cycles to a finite-flat open and pushes flat inverse images forward. Useful nonrational coprime-index examples are not asserted.
cor:finite-index-chow.conclusion: Over every field extension the degree map on CH0 is surjective and its kernel is annihilated by gcd(d_i); coprime indices imply universal CH0-triviality.
cor:finite-index-chow.hypotheses: Characteristic zero and one or more constructions satisfying every hypothesis of the finite-index theorem, with indices d_i.
cor:finite-index-chow.objects: Smooth proper models of a geometrically integral variety birational to quotients admitting finite-index slices.

cor:generic-surface-level.cautions: The function-field identification and the upper-bound rationalization base-change from Q(t). No unchanged Galois type after extension is assumed; the lower bound uses the specified cubic, not arbitrary quartic del Pezzo surfaces.
cor:generic-surface-level.hypotheses: F has characteristic zero; j is 1 or 3; S_j is the actual generic contracted surface in the TZ cubic fibration.
cor:generic-surface-level.objects: The generic quartic del Pezzo surfaces S_j over Q(t) associated with the two specified cubic threefolds, and their base changes to F(t).

cor:moduli.cautions: The finite value is proved only for X_1 and X_3; the infinite value is a very-general statement.
cor:moduli.conclusion: The function ell_C is two on the displayed cubic examples and infinite at a very general point.
cor:moduli.hypotheses: The base field is C and the cubic is either displayed or very general as specified.
cor:moduli.objects: The level-of-stable-rationality function ell_C on smooth cubic-threefold moduli.

cor:partner-level.cautions: The birational correspondence over F is a hypothesis. It is not constructed for every threefold or every genus-eight Fano.
cor:partner-level.hypotheses: F has characteristic zero and V times P1 is F-birational to X_j times P1 for j=1 or 3.
cor:partner-level.objects: A geometrically integral threefold V/F and one specified cubic X_j after extension to F.

cor:rational-pencil-partners.cautions: Finite necessary candidate set, not an implemented solver or exact classification; no assertion for all complex parameters.
cor:rational-pencil-partners.conclusion: Only finitely many rational parameters can be partners.
cor:rational-pencil-partners.hypotheses: Fix a nonzero rational parameter in this pencil.
cor:rational-pencil-partners.objects: Rational parameters with isogenous intermediate Jacobian or birational first stabilization.

cor:torus-linearization-level.cautions: Uses the cubic lower and upper bounds. These are rational actions, not regular polynomial actions. The existence of nonlinearizable rank-two examples was already known to Popov.
cor:torus-linearization-level.conclusion: Exact trivial-stabilization levels two for the rank-two action and one for each rank-one restriction; every finite-subgroup quotient over C is rational.
cor:torus-linearization-level.hypotheses: Characteristic-zero ground field; the two cubic level theorem; adjoined variables fixed by the torus. Finite-subgroup conclusion over C.
cor:torus-linearization-level.objects: Rational rank-two torus actions on affine five-space from the two exact-level-two cubics.

lem:universal-tangent-cover.cautions: Finite nonemptiness over the splitting field only. General tangent-projection compatibility and ground-field existence remain in prop:tangent-section. No Lean coverage is claimed.
lem:universal-tangent-cover.conclusion: At least one witness has a smooth tangent point, four-dimensional H_p and invertible evaluation; the four determinant/minor opens cover all smooth parameters.
lem:universal-tangent-cover.hypotheses: Algebraically closed field of characteristic zero; Delta = ab(a-1)(b-1)(a-b) is nonzero.
lem:universal-tangent-cover.objects: The four split Cox-coordinate witness pairs, tangent hyperplane spaces, evaluation determinants and Jacobian minors.

prop:fibration-level.cautions: The surface hypotheses are imposed over the generic function field. If ell(B) is at most four, the formula gives only an upper bound of two for ell(Y), not an exact value.
prop:fibration-level.conclusion: Y times A2 is k-birational to B times A4; max(ell(Y)-2,0)=max(ell(B)-4,0), including infinity, with the stated finite-level consequences and equivalence of stable rationality.
prop:fibration-level.hypotheses: The field has characteristic zero; the generic fibre is birational over k(B) to a smooth quartic del Pezzo surface with a rational point and stably permutation geometric Picard lattice.
prop:fibration-level.objects: A dominant rational map Y to B of geometrically integral varieties and their stabilization levels.

prop:pencil-local-rank.cautions: Use geometric isogeny and potential reduction, not original-field conductor or untwisted Frobenius traces.
prop:pencil-local-rank.conclusion: Smoothness and ranks 1 at numerator primes, 3 at discriminant primes, 0 otherwise.
prop:pencil-local-rank.hypotheses: Nonzero reduced rational t=a/b, b>0, p>=5.
prop:pencil-local-rank.objects: Intermediate Jacobian and eventual semistable toric ranks of the rational pencil.

prop:rank-four-descent.cautions: Exact program-checked lattice assertions and a descent proof in the text, not a Lean theorem. This excludes only the stated weight-space criterion in this embedding with full I3, not other embeddings, nonlinear sections, or smaller Galois images.
prop:rank-four-descent.conclusion: There is a unique rank-four subtorus; its sixteen distinct coordinate weights have orbits of size four and twelve, so no sum of five weight spaces descends.
prop:rank-four-descent.hypotheses: The projective Cox embedding is fixed and the Galois image is the full group I3.
prop:rank-four-descent.objects: Rank-four subtori of the projective Cox torus with its full marked I3 Galois action.

prop:tangent-section.cautions: The subgroup classification is complete only for the four types for which H1 vanishes on every subgroup; no classification of all W(D5) subgroups is claimed.
prop:tangent-section.conclusion: Geometrically, there is a codimension-three tangent linear section containing a point x on the quotient component where tangent projection is an isomorphism. For each of the four types, the points and the section descend when the surface has a rational point.
prop:tangent-section.hypotheses: The ground field has characteristic zero and the Cox parameters lie on the smooth open; for ground-field descent the quartic del Pezzo surface has a rational point and the Galois image has type I0, I1, I2, or I3.
prop:tangent-section.objects: The saturated rank-three subtorus, complementary Cox-coordinate subspace, and the incidence conditions defining the tangent section.

rem:fano-partners.cautions: No arithmetic descent of Kuznetsov's correspondence and no exact-level result for every genus-eight Fano is asserted.
rem:fano-partners.conclusion: The partner corollary gives exact level two for these specified partners.
rem:fano-partners.hypotheses: Kuznetsov works over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. Over other fields the required projective-bundle correspondence must be defined over the ground field.
rem:fano-partners.objects: Smooth genus-eight Fano threefolds with one of the specified cubics as associated Pfaffian cubic.

rem:finite-index-scroll.cautions: Explicit algebraic formulas in the text, not a computer certificate or Lean formalization. The quotient is already rational; this is not a new nonrational coprime-index example.
rem:finite-index-scroll.conclusion: The hypotheses of the finite-index theorem hold with index two and rational component degree one.
rem:finite-index-scroll.hypotheses: Characteristic zero, the specified weight spaces, point (1,1), hyperplane, and witness (2,-1).
rem:finite-index-scroll.objects: The O(1,2) embedding of P1 times P1 and the effective torus scaling its second factor.

rem:saturation.cautions: The degree-two artifact belongs to the parameter isogeny, not the Rosenlicht quotient.
rem:saturation.conclusion: Adjoining the half-sum saturates the cocharacter lattice and removes the projective mu_2 kernel.
rem:saturation.hypotheses: The three pairwise-sign cocharacters are used in the last three coordinates.
rem:saturation.objects: An index-two even-sum cocharacter sublattice and its saturation.

thm:cubic-level.cautions: The upper bound base-changes from Q. The lower bound descends a putative birational map, its inverse, and their identities to a finitely generated subfield before embedding into C; F itself need not embed into C.
thm:cubic-level.hypotheses: F has characteristic zero and X is one of the two displayed smooth cubic threefolds.
thm:cubic-level.objects: The least rational stabilization of either specified cubic after extension from Q to an arbitrary characteristic-zero field F.

thm:finite-index-slice.cautions: The proof uses transversality for dominance and a constant finite-kernel torsor after algebraic closure of constants for divisibility. Index d need not equal the component degree e; no geometric component is assumed to descend.
thm:finite-index-slice.conclusion: The closure of the section on the tangent-isomorphism open is geometrically integral and k-rational, dominates the quotient, and has degree e dividing d.
thm:finite-index-slice.hypotheses: Characteristic zero and all hypotheses of the unimodular quotient criterion, replacing the basis condition by a sublattice of finite index d.
thm:finite-index-slice.objects: A generically free projectively linear torus action, selected weights, tangent projection and descended linear section.

thm:separated-pencil.cautions: Separation of products imports rational Hodge conservation. Density is elementary; no height theorem or all-parameter cancellation.
thm:separated-pencil.conclusion: Jacobians geometrically nonisogenous, first stabilizations nonbirational over C, second stabilizations rational over Q; density 3/pi^2.
thm:separated-pencil.hypotheses: Positive distinct squarefree integers prime to six.
thm:separated-pencil.objects: Squarefree integral parameters in the explicit cubic pencil.

thm:torus-quotient.cautions: A finite-index set of weight differences would give a finite orbit cover and does not suffice.
thm:torus-quotient.conclusion: The Rosenlicht quotient Z/T is k-rational.
thm:torus-quotient.hypotheses: A generically free projectively linear rank-r torus action, a rational point in the birational tangent-projection locus, descended complementary sums of projective weight spaces, an integral basis of weight differences, and a nondegenerate tangent linear section whose quotient component meets the tangent-projection isomorphism open.
thm:torus-quotient.objects: A projective torus action on a projective variety and its Rosenlicht quotient.

thm:two-variable.cautions: Universal-torsor geometry and the four-type classification are imported from Tschinkel--Zhang.
thm:two-variable.conclusion: S times A2 and S times P2 are k-rational; this applies to every stably k-rational S.
thm:two-variable.hypotheses: Characteristic zero, S smooth quartic del Pezzo, S(k) nonempty, and geometric Picard lattice stably permutation.
thm:two-variable.objects: A quartic del Pezzo surface and a two-dimensional stabilization.

thm:uniform-cubic-family.cautions: Upper bound independent of companion; lower bound imported. Signed Picard representation checked in text; moduli rank is exact symbolic computation.
thm:uniform-cubic-family.conclusion: Exact level two after every extension; complex moduli image dimension three.
thm:uniform-cubic-family.hypotheses: Characteristic-zero k; lambda,mu,nu in k; cubic smooth; any K/k. Moduli-image clause concerns the parameter family over C.
thm:uniform-cubic-family.objects: Smooth displayed three-parameter cubic and its complex moduli image.
